tasks.title: List remote images
tasks.instructions:
List the Ubuntu images available on the `ubuntu:` remote:

```bash
lxc image list ubuntu:
```

This shows all available Ubuntu images. You can also search for a specific version:

```bash
lxc image list ubuntu:24.04
```
hints: The output shows aliases, fingerprints, and sizes for each image.
You can filter by appending a search term after the remote.

tasks.title: Launch from a specific image
tasks.instructions:
Launch a container named `app` from the Ubuntu 24.04 image:

```bash
lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 app
```

Verify it's running:
```bash
lxc list
```
hints: If the image is already cached, this will be fast.
The container should appear in RUNNING state in lxc list.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc launch ubuntu:24.04 app
lxc list
```

tasks.title: List local images
tasks.instructions:
List the images cached on your local LXD server:

```bash
lxc image list
```

You should see at least one Ubuntu 24.04 image (from the previous task). Note the fingerprint or alias — you'll need it in the next task.
hints: lxc image list (without a remote prefix) shows local images only.
Look for the ALIAS and FINGERPRINT columns in the output.

tasks.title: Publish a custom image
tasks.instructions:
Create a custom image from the `app` container:

1. Stop the container:
```bash
lxc stop app
```

2. Publish it as a new image with alias `my-app`:
```bash
lxc publish app --alias my-app
```

3. Verify the image was created:
```bash
lxc image list
```

You should see `my-app` in the ALIAS column.
hints: Containers must be stopped before publishing.
lxc publish <instance> --alias <name> creates a new local image.
The new image will appear in lxc image list with the alias 'my-app'.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc stop app
lxc publish app --alias my-app
lxc image list
```

tasks.title: Launch from your custom image
tasks.instructions:
Launch a new container from the custom image you just created:

```bash
lxc launch my-app app-clone
```

Verify it's running:
```bash
lxc list
```

You should see both `app` (stopped) and `app-clone` (running).
hints: You can launch from a local image alias just like from a remote image.
The new container should be an exact copy of 'app' when the image was published.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc launch my-app app-clone
lxc list
```
